topIssues.title: l1-watcher: a transient L1 RPC failure on one chain kills the whole node
topIssues.author: claude
topIssues.body:
In the kona-node L1 watcher, one chain's failure is fatal to the whole node. When a chain's `eth_getLogs` request for system config logs fails — a transient L1 RPC error is enough — or a chain's derivation channel is closed, `L1WatcherActor::step` (`rust/kona/crates/node/service/src/actors/l1_watcher/actor.rs`) returns `Err`. The actor runner at `rust/kona/crates/node/service/src/service/util.rs:33` treats any actor error as fatal: it cancels every actor, and the host exits.

This predates the multi-chain watcher change in #22567 — a single-chain kona-node dies the same way when its L1 RPC hiccups, and transient L1 failures should never kill the node. At N > 1 chains served by one watcher the blast radius grows: one chain's transient L1 error stops every other chain in the host.

From the review discussion on #22567 (https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22567#discussion_r3838547816):

> Indeed this seems like a bug in even the current kona-node because transient L1 failures should never kill the node. We should log an issue for this and then create a follow up PR to fix it properly.

A follow-up PR will add per-chain fault handling: transient RPC errors retried or skipped rather than propagated as fatal, and per-chain isolation so one chain's failure does not stop the others.

Part of #22531.

topIssues.title: [PCD] Default-`X` benchmarking
topIssues.author: 0xOneTony
topIssues.body: `X` (the offset between the chosen L1 anchor's timestamp and the committed L2 `genesis_time`) must be large enough that `genesis_time` is still in the future when `OPCM.deploy()` is mined; otherwise `op-node` will produce empty filler blocks at L2 block time to fill the gap. Measure end-to-end runtime of the off-chain portion of the pipeline (anchor selection through prestate generation) against a real prestate builder, repeated enough times to get a stable result. Propose a default `X`.

topIssues.title: kona-node: --sequencer.max-safe-lag and --conductor.rpc.timeout are parsed but silently ignored
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
## Summary

kona-node accepts two sequencer CLI flags that have no effect: they are parsed into `SequencerArgs` but never make it into `SequencerConfig`, so an operator setting them gets silent no-ops instead of an error.

| Flag | Env | Declared | Dropped |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--sequencer.max-safe-lag` | `KONA_NODE_SEQUENCER_MAX_SAFE_LAG` | [`flags/sequencer.rs#L24-L31`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/68b009443f/rust/kona/bin/node/src/flags/sequencer.rs#L24-L31) | [`SequencerArgs::config()`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/68b009443f/rust/kona/bin/node/src/flags/sequencer.rs#L70-L77) |
| `--conductor.rpc.timeout` | `KONA_NODE_CONDUCTOR_RPC_TIMEOUT` | [`flags/sequencer.rs#L50-L57`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/68b009443f/rust/kona/bin/node/src/flags/sequencer.rs#L50-L57) | same; [`SequencerConfig`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/68b009443f/rust/kona/crates/node/service/src/actors/sequencer/config.rs#L10-L19) has no timeout field and [`ConductorClient::new_http`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/68b009443f/rust/kona/crates/node/service/src/actors/sequencer/conductor.rs#L50-L53) builds the client without one |

`grep -rn 'max_safe_lag\|conductor_rpc_timeout' rust/kona` finds no reader outside the flag definitions.

## Impact

- `--conductor.rpc.timeout` defaults to 1s and is documented as a timeout, but the conductor `commit_unsafe_payload` call on the sequencer's seal path ([`sequencer/actor.rs#L197-L204`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/68b009443f/rust/kona/crates/node/service/src/actors/sequencer/actor.rs#L197-L204)) runs with no timeout at all — a slow or hung conductor blocks block production indefinitely.
- `--sequencer.max-safe-lag` is a silent no-op; the feature itself is tracked in #22266. Until it is implemented, the flag should either be removed or fail loudly.

## Suggested fix

- Thread `conductor_rpc_timeout` into `SequencerConfig` and apply it to the conductor client (or wrap the RPC calls in `tokio::time::timeout`).
- Either implement `max_safe_lag` (#22266) or drop the flag; do not keep accepting it.

Related: #22266, #21906.

topPRs.title: Silhouette: private interoperable chains (v1, attested)
topPRs.author: opsuperchain
topPRs.body:
## Silhouette: private interoperable chains (v1, attested) A silhouette chain is a private L2 that participates in an ordinary interop dependency set. Its transactions stay private. L1 carries a signed proof envelope describing the chain's public outline and a standard derivation carrier with user transactions removed. v1 is explicitly operator-attested: the trusted submitter's L1 signature authenticates the claimed state. The wire reserves a proof slot for a future proven mode, but this PR contains no ZK toolchain or L1 settlement path. ### Architecture - **No `op-node` changes.** The final PR diff under `op-node/` is empty. - **No custom submitter.** The normal `op-batcher` loads real private blocks, receipts and output roots and retains its normal channel, reorg, txmgr and retry lifecycle. A terminal encoder emits the silhouette proof envelope followed by standard carrier frames for the same block cadence with user transactions removed. - **Normal inbox and stock portal.** Both envelope and carrier go to the rollup's normal batch inbox. Deposits remain enabled and are stock-derived; there is no gated portal contract. - **Stock derivation.** A stock verifier `op-node` ignores the `KCPB` proof blob as an unknown derivation format, consumes the following standard carrier frames, and runs the ordinary Holocene/interop rewind and deposits-only replacement path. - **One verifier-only supernode role.** Silhouette chains cannot be sequenced by a supernode virtual node. Private sequencing is performed by a LightCL op-node backed by the private EL. - **Standalone magic EL.** `op-silhouette-el` is an in-memory Engine/eth RPC service. It watches the authenticated proof stream independently, maps stock carrier attributes to proof-committed block hashes and roots, and delegates a stock deposits-only replacement build to the private EL when interop invalidates a proven block. - **Normal interop semantics.** The supernode's stock judge validates the private chain's declared imports against independently derived public-chain messages. Invalid blocks are replaced and transitive invalidation propagates across chains. ### What is posted to L1 Each normal batcher submission contains: 1. `KCPB` envelope magic, wire version, public-values length/data, and proof length/data (empty in attested mode). 2. Batch commitments: previous/new output root, L1 head hash, rollup-config hash, dependency-set hash, export-policy hash, and the block list. 3. Per block: number, timestamp, real block hash, state root, message-passer storage root, exported logs, imported messages, L1-origin hash/number, and sequence number. 4. Per exported log: real block log index, log hash, and optional preimage (empty under the default all-hashes policy). 5. Per imported message: origin, source block/log index/timestamp/chain ID, and payload hash. 6. Standard compressed derivation channel/frame data carrying each block's parent, epoch, timestamp, stock deposits/L1-info transaction, and an empty user-transaction list. It does **not** publish private user transaction bytes or hashes, senders, calldata, receipts, contract state, or full log contents. The ordinary L1 blob transaction still exposes its sender, destination inbox, nonce, fees, commitments and inclusion block. ### Images Build these three branch-specific targets: ```sh docker buildx bake op-batcher op-supernode op-silhouette-el ``` | Image | Difference from a normal interop deployment | |---|---| | `op-batcher` | Enables the terminal silhouette proof + stripped-carrier encoding. | | `op-supernode` | Loads the silhouette verifier manifest and proof observer. It remains verifier-only. | | `op-silhouette-el` | New in-memory proof-backed Engine/eth service used as P's verifier EL. | The standalone `op-node`, L1/L2 execution clients, and portal contracts are stock. There is no `proofbatch-submitter` image. ### Minimal configuration delta Private producer: ```sh op-batcher --data-availability-type blobs --silhouette \ --max-pending-tx 1 --target-num-frames 6 \ --silhouette.inbox $NORMAL_BATCH_INBOX --silhouette.wire-version 4 \ --silhouette.rollup-config-hash $ROLLUP_HASH \ --silhouette.dependency-set-hash $DEPSET_HASH ``` The producer is otherwise a normal LightCL sequencer + private EL. It uses the stock `OptimismPortal`; the silhouette inbox must equal the normal rollup batch inbox. Magic EL: ```sh op-silhouette-el --l1 $L1_RPC --l1.beacon $L1_BEACON \ --supernode $SUPERNODE_RPC --rollup-config rollup-p.json \ --verifier-config verifier-p.json \ --replacement-engine $PRIVATE_ENGINE_AUTH_RPC \ --replacement-engine.jwt-secret jwt.txt --rpc.addr 0.0.0.0 --rpc.port 9545 ``` Verifier supernode: ```sh op-supernode --silhouette manifest.json \ --vn.

.l2 http://op-silhouette-el:9545 \ --vn.

.interop.dependency-set depset.json ``` The `op-node` VN has no silhouette/private flag: its only unusual input is that its configured EL endpoint speaks the proof-backed Engine API. The manifest names P's verifier config; A is absent and remains an ordinary chain. The verifier config binds L1 chain ID, trusted submitter, normal inbox, rollup/dependency-set hashes, `proofType: "attested"`, `wireVersion: 4`, and the anchor. ### Local network and smoke tests ```sh go run ./op-up --silhouette # funded transactional RPCs: A http://127.0.0.1:8545, B http://127.0.0.1:8546 go run ./op-up smoke-interop all go run ./op-up smoke-interop invalid-message --direction both --reorg-timeout 5m go run ./op-up smoke-interop chained-invalid-message --require-cascade --reorg-timeout 5m # comparison topology go run ./op-up --interop ``` Observed locally on this revision: - silhouette `smoke-interop all`: PASS; - bidirectional invalid A→B and B→A: both replaced and both chains resumed; - strict chained invalidation: invalid P block, direct dependent, and descendant dependent all reorged while the independent control remained; - normal sysgo bidirectional invalid smoke: same replacement/resume semantics (lower latency because it does not wait for the proof-batch cadence); - focused `TestSilhouetteImportThatIsFalseIsReplaced`: PASS; - `op-batcher`, all `op-supernode`, sysgo/presets, smoke utility, and `op-up` unit suites: PASS. The serialized full silhouette acceptance package still has one known timeout in `TestSilhouetteCrossChainPinsThenAdvances`; the replacement regression and proof-slot refusal tests pass independently. ### Diff size Against the PR base: approximately **24.3k insertions / 1.45k deletions across 267 files**. Much of the file count is the existing cross-language fixture corpus. The architecture rewrite in the latest commit is **3,487 insertions / 7,004 deletions**: it deletes the custom submitter, sequencing-side silhouette role, custom portal, and op-node hook in favor of the stock paths above. Operational details and the exact trust statement live in `op-supernode/silhouette/docs/RUNNING-V1.md` and `TRUST-MODEL.md`.

topPRs.title: kona-node,op-reth,op-batcher: multi-blocks PoC (up to max_multi_blocks blocks per block time)
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
**Draft / PoC, work in progress — CI feedback only for now.**

Multi-blocks: keep `block_time`, allow the sequencer to build up to `max_multi_blocks` L2 blocks sharing one timestamp after a feature timestamp `multi_block_time` (≥ Karst, not a hardfork). Sealing policy is the builder's choice; consensus only bounds the group size. Chain consistency is parent-hash linkage.

Scope of the PoC: kona-node (sequencer + derivation), op-reth (EL), op-batcher (span batch v2), op-devstack + acceptance tests on a kona-node/op-reth-only devnet. op-node keeps rejecting span batch v2; interop, proofs, flashblocks and registry support are out of scope.

Landed so far (one commit per workstream):
- op-reth: `ts == parent.ts` accepted iff siblings are allowed at `ts`; builder seal policy flags; `engine_awaitPayloadReadyV1`
- kona: `multi_block_time`/`max_multi_blocks` config; `BatchType::SpanV2` = Delta span + `same_ts_bits` (bit 0 = sibling of the span's parent, so groups may straddle spans/channels)
- Go: rollup/deploy config, span batch v2 codec + `SpanChannelOut` switch, devstack options and DSL helpers, shared golden vectors

Still to come: kona derivation validity, kona sequencer slot loop, acceptance tests.

Judgement calls worth a look:
- the `min-build-time` policy only seals a payload that holds ≥ 1 user tx, so an idle sequencer still makes one block per block time
- straddling groups across span batches/channels is allowed (bit 0), instead of forcing the batcher to keep groups atomic across L1-driven channel closes
- `siblings_allowed` is false at *every* configured fork activation timestamp, which keeps the timestamp-only `is_first_<fork>_block` predicates correct for forks scheduled after activation

topPRs.title: op-reth,kona: implement sequencer-defined fees
topPRs.author: joshklop
topPRs.body:
## Description

Implement Sequencer-Defined Fees (SDF) at Lagoon. The sequencer selects `baseFeePerGas` through a pluggable policy, commits that selection in the trailing `PostExec` transaction, and validators reproduce execution from the committed fee without running producer policy.

This change:

- extends the unactivated version-1 `PostExec` payload with the selected base fee
- requires a trailing Lagoon commitment, including for empty refund sets
- wires fee selection and immutable per-payload caching through op-reth payload building
- uses selected-fee quotes in txpool, pending execution, and fee-related RPC paths
- validates Lagoon commitments on Engine API block import
- reproduces fallback commitments in Kona and preserves them in output artifacts
- applies selected fees during flashblock replay and reserves block space for the mandatory commitment
- updates public documentation and acceptance-test expectations

L1 data fees, operator fees, batch formats, and payload-attribute schemas are unchanged.

## Dependencies

- Depends on ethereum-optimism/reth#8. The Rust workspace is pinned to that PR's organization-owned branch revision while it is under review.
- Specification: ethereum-optimism/specs#934.
- Premium policy integration: ethereum-optimism/optimism-premium#222.

## Validation

Completed before opening this draft:

- full Go lint and Optimism Rust lint on the initial series
- targeted op-reth/Kona tests, including 41 Kona executor tests
- no-std checks and nightly formatting
- focused checks for consensus, Kona executor/driver, flashblocks, payload builder, and RPC against the public reth revision
- regression tests for Engine API commitment validation, Kona fallback transaction persistence, flashblock selected-fee execution, and block-size reservation

Final review, broader validation after the latest fixes, and CI follow-up are still in progress.

## Review notes

Earlier independent review findings about the Engine API validation path, Kona fallback artifacts, flashblock fees, historical fee history, fill-transaction defaults, and block-size accounting were addressed before this draft was opened.

Dismissed findings:

- Cached policy failures are intentional: a payload ID has one immutable policy resolution across retries.
- A `PostExec` version 2 is unnecessary because version 1 has not activated onchain.
- Extending op-geth is out of scope because Lagoon follows the op-geth support horizon.
- No span-batch format change is required; span batches already transport the transaction bytes.

topPRs.title: kona-engine: mirror op-node sync regimes to fix the sync-tester verifier livelock
topPRs.author: claude
topPRs.body:
<!-- ccr-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **Sebastian Stammler** · [Slack thread](https://oplabs-pbc.slack.com/archives/C0BHEH8TG91/p1787240090382769)_

Fixes the livelock behind all five failing `sync_tester` acceptance tests (`op-acceptance-tests/tests/supernode/sync_tester/`) by mirroring op-node's behaviour, per the governing rule for lokahi. Part of #22537.

## Before

All five tests timed out at ~720s in a single livelock, spamming >50MB of paired warnings (`sync_tester.go:185` "Requested block is ahead of sync tester state" / kona "Failed to fetch unsafe l2 block for consolidation") at ~5k attempts/s:

1. Kona adopted gossiped tips the EL answered SYNCING for regardless of sync phase (`insert/task.rs`, `synchronize/task.rs:94-98`), so the unsafe head named blocks the EL could not serve.
2. Consolidation's fetch of such a block surfaced as `FailedToFetchUnsafeL2Block` → **Temporary** (`consolidate/error.rs`), retried forever with no realignment and no pacing (`tasks/task.rs` retried with only a `yield_now`).
3. On a cold restart, nothing ever put a forkchoice update on the wire until gossip did, so against a reset sync-tester session (CLSync, sequencer far ahead) EL sync never "finished" and derivation never started at all.

## After — per gap, with the op-node behaviour being mirrored

**G1 — consolidation fetch miss → op-node's stall/reset split** (`kona-engine`, commit 1)
- Rust: `consolidate/task.rs` + `consolidate/error.rs`: a miss is now `AwaitingELSyncUnsafeL2Block` (Temporary) while `!el_sync_finished`, and `MissingUnsafeL2Block` (Reset — walkback realigns the unsafe head, then the gate flips to force-building) after. Not-found-shaped RPC error responses fold into the miss.
- Go: `op-node/rollup/attributes/attributes.go:204-221` (NotFound → EL-sync stall vs `rollup.ResetEvent`), `:222-227` (other errors Temporary), `:185-193` (post-reset force-build gate), `op-service/eth/errors.go:10-27` (`MaybeAsNotFoundErr` hardening). The string set is a documented **superset** of op-node's (bare `"not found"` included): kona adopts optimistic heads and so fetches ahead of the EL where op-node's payload queue never would, and the sync tester answers that miss with a bare `not found` error (`sync_tester.go:183-187`).

**G2 — REVISED after CI (commit 2 shipped a gate, commit 6 removed it): the gossip EL-sync channel stays open past the initial sync**
- The first version refused SYNCING unsafe heads once `el_sync_finished` was set, mirroring op-node's CL-sync regime. CI proved that wrong for kona: op-node's CL-sync mode has reqresp sync and an unsafe payload queue to catch up with; kona has neither, so adopting the gossiped tip and pointing the EL at it is its *only* unsafe-chain catch-up channel — and a verifier that falls behind (restart, dropped peer) re-enters it after the initial sync. The gate stranded such verifiers forever: `rust-e2e-restart` `TestSequencerRestart`, `rust-e2e-simple-kona` `TestSyncUnsafeBecomesSafe`, and the 7 kona CL-sync acceptance tests (`TestUnsafeChainNotStalling_*`, `TestCLELDivergence`, `TestGlamsterdamP2PUnsafeBlockBecomesSafe`) all failed on the new drop log.
- Final behaviour: op-node's EL-sync regime in both phases (`engine_controller.go:587-594`, `sync_deriver.go:102-115`) — unchanged from develop. The sync-tester livelock is instead broken where op-node breaks it: at G1's consolidation fetch-miss reset, which realigns the unsafe head with the EL and flips the gate to force-building (`attributes.go:185-193, 204-221`).

**G3 — paced temporary retries** (`kona-engine`, commit 3)
- Rust: `tasks/task.rs`: exponential backoff (100ms base, 10s cap) instead of a bare `yield_now` in the Temporary retry loop.
- Go: `op-node/rollup/driver/step_scheduling_deriver.go:97-109` + `op-service/retry/strategies.go:49-55` (`retry.Exponential()`, capped at 10s).

**Startup — op-node's initial reset** (`kona-node-service` + `kona-engine`, commit 4)
- Rust: `chain_controller/controller.rs`: the controller's first step runs the walkback reset — but only against an EL that reports a **finalized block**, op-node's own EL-sync discriminator ("the engine has no finalized block until its initial snap-sync completes", `engine_controller.go:597-624`; EL sync is only entered "if there is no finalized block", `:29`). A fresh EL (no finalized label — every real EL in the short-lived e2e/acceptance suites, where nothing finalizes) is left to the gossip bootstrap exactly as on develop; the sync-tester EL always serves its finalized label, so the probe runs there, derivation starts at once, and the cold-restart CLSync deadlock is gone. The probe's FCU doubles as the EL-sync marker (VALID → derivation starts; SYNCING → bootstrap unchanged), and a walkback the EL cannot serve falls back to the gossip bootstrap rather than failing startup. `task_queue/core.rs`: `Engine::reset` now retries RPC-level walkback failures with backoff instead of returning them — which previously killed the requesting actor (and the node) when the EL was merely unavailable at startup (`ResetForkchoiceError("An RPC error occurred: client error (SendRequest)")`, the `startup_resync` `ConnectsAfterELUnavailableAtStartup` failure).
- Go: `op-node/rollup/derive/pipeline.go:181-190, 224` (`initialReset` at startup in every sync mode), `op-node/rollup/engine/engine_controller.go:1423-1432` (reset request → `FindL2Heads` walkback; a failure re-emits the reset event rather than dying), `op-node/rollup/driver/sync_deriver.go:225-230`.

Note: the devstack deliberately passes no sync mode to lokahi (`op-devstack/sysgo/multichain_supernode_runtime.go:711-714`), so kona keeps its modeless design. The regime selection is now behavioural rather than keyed on `el_sync_finished`: an EL with no finalized block gets the gossip EL-sync bootstrap (op-node's EL-sync mode), one with chain state gets the startup walkback probe (op-node's startup `initialReset`), and either way the unsafe-gossip channel stays open — a non-syncing EL (the sync tester's CL-sync sessions) converges through consolidation-miss resets plus derivation force-builds instead of livelocking. Expected trade: against such an EL the node performs a walkback reset per missed-gossip stretch (bounded by the paced retries and cheap re-derivation from the last safe head) — the honest cost of modelessness; an explicit sync-mode flag remains the follow-up if that churn matters in practice.

## Round 2: the receipts wedge (after the fixes above)

With the engine-layer fixes in, CI (job 5518771) showed the old livelock and reset churn gone and derivation healthy — but all five tests still timed out on their first `CheckAll`, because **interop verification could not parse the sync-tester's receipts**, so cross-safe never left 0 (and with interop active, the DSL-visible safe/finalized heads only move on cross-safe promotions):

- The sync tester served `eth_getBlockReceipts` by round-tripping the upstream EL's response through geth's consensus `types.Receipt` (`op-sync-tester/synctester/frontend/eth.go:34-35` via `backend/el_reader.go:72-73`), a type with no `from`/`to` fields — silently stripping fields the execution-apis spec requires and every real EL serves.
- alloy's `TransactionReceipt` requires `from` (alloy-rpc-types-eth-1.8.3 `receipt.rs:64`), so lokahi's verifier failed deserialization on the first block's receipts, the error classified transient (`rust/lokahi/src/interop/chain.rs` → `ChainError::Unreachable`), retried every ~2s for the full 720s budget.
- The Go stack never noticed: op-node/op-supervisor decode receipts into the same lossy geth type (`op-service/sources/receipts_rpc.go:96`), which is why the op-node twins of these tests pass against the same sync-tester EL in the same job.

Two commits:

1. **`op-sync-tester`: raw receipts passthrough** (primary) — `eth_getBlockReceipts` now relays the raw payload from the read-only EL, exactly like the existing `GetBlockByNumberJSON`/`GetBlockByHashJSON` accessors; the session ahead-of-state gate reads only `blockNumber` out of the raw JSON. The regression test pins that `from`/`to` survive through both the backend and the RPC frontend. This makes the harness faithful to real ELs for every client.
2. **`lokahi`: lenient receipt read in the verifier** (hardening) — `block_logs` only consumes logs, so it now fetches `eth_getBlockReceipts` into a logs-only local type instead of alloy's full typed receipt. This mirrors the Go stack's posture (op-geth's `Receipt` has no `from` at all): a receipt shape the Go verifier accepts must not wedge this one. The unit test deserializes the CI-captured geth-shaped receipt (no `from`) and extracts its logs.

## Round 3: two more harness-vs-spec and mirroring gaps (after the receipts fix)

With the receipts fix in (job 5519251), `AdvancesViaSyncTester` passes; the four remaining failures split into two root causes:

**Activation pair — Lagoon upgrade-gas strip asymmetry (`kona-protocol`).** Both attribute builders add only the NUT bundle's gas to a single-chain Interop activation block (kona `stateful.rs` `upgrade_gas_for_activation(false)`; op-node `interop_activation_transactions.go:37-61`), but kona's `to_system_config` stripped the *multi-chain* amount (bundle + 150k setFeature/ETHLiquidity wrappers) back out — reconstructing a gas limit 150k below the real one, so every attribute set built from the activation block onward was rejected with `-38003 gaslimit mismatch: attr=59850000, header=60000000` and the build task retried at the queue head forever. op-node strips `UpgradeGas(forks.Lagoon)` = bundle-only (`payload_util.go:62-80`, `upgrade_transaction.go:158-168`); kona now does the same. Fail-first test round-trips a single-chain activation block back to the steady-state limit.

**FromCold pair — sync-tester `engine_getPayload` responses were not spec-shaped (`op-sync-tester`).** The tester served its stored `eth.ExecutionPayloadEnvelope` (gossip shape: executionPayload + parentBeaconBlockRoot only) from every getPayload version. The spec requires `blockValue` (V2+), `blobsBundle`/`shouldOverrideBuilder`/`parentBeaconBlockRoot` (V3+), `executionRequests` (V4+); Go clients decode into the same lossy type and never noticed, but kona (getPayloadV5 → `OpExecutionPayloadEnvelopeV4`) hard-fails on the missing `blockValue` — so after a cold restart (session reset to Latest:0, every block force-built) sealing block 1 retried forever and nothing ever advanced. Same class as the receipts bug; same style of fix: the RPC frontend now wraps the stored envelope into the per-version spec response (blockValue 0, empty-but-present blobs bundle, empty executionRequests), payload untouched, Go clients unaffected. The `requested=62` / `BlockRetrievalFailed` spam was a symptom: the interop verifier's persisted DB polling a pre-restart block until the chain catches up. Fail-first frontend test pins the per-version field sets and non-null arrays.

Round-3 verification: `cargo nextest -p kona-protocol` (256) and `-p kona-derive` (206) green including the new round-trip tests; `go test ./op-sync-tester/...` green including the new getPayload shape test; clippy/fmt clean on the touched crates.

## Verification

- Round 2: `go test ./op-sync-tester/...` green (incl. the new from/to passthrough regression test); `cargo nextest -p lokahi` green (incl. the captured-receipt leniency test).
- Fail-first unit tests in every touched area: consolidate miss split and not-found mapping (bare `"not found"` included), SYNCING FCU/insert adoption in both EL-sync phases (pinning the catch-up channel the CI regression removed), temporary-retry backoff timing, `Engine::reset` walkback retry, controller startup probe (probe, finalized-gated skip, and walkback-failure fallback).
- `cargo nextest run -p kona-engine -p kona-node-service -p lokahi`: 391 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p kona-engine -p kona-node-service -p lokahi -p kona-node --all-features --all-targets`: clean.
- Nightly `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean. Docs lint (rustdoc `-D warnings`) for the touched crates: clean.
- Not run here (please run in CI / locally): the `sync_tester` acceptance suite itself — building its full dependency set exceeded this environment's disk budget.
- Repo review agents (`rust-code-reviewer`): not run — this worker session cannot spawn the repo's review agents; flagged per the contribution guide instead of skipping silently.

topPRs.title: op-challenger: delete withdrawal proofs invalidated by challenger wins
topPRs.author: claude
topPRs.body:
<!-- ccr-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **Adrian Sutton** · [Slack thread](https://oplabs-pbc.slack.com/archives/C0BTT5DGHA4/p1787791642391549?thread_ts=1787791642.391549&cid=C0BTT5DGHA4)_

Stacks on #22669.

**Before:** #22669 makes `deleteProvenWithdrawal` permissionless once the game a withdrawal was proven against resolves as `CHALLENGER_WINS`, but nothing calls it. Those proofs can never finalize, yet they stay in `provenWithdrawals` and keep counting toward `numProofSubmitters`, so anything reading the portal still sees a live proof against an invalid game.

**After:** op-challenger deletes them automatically. The feature is off unless `--optimism-portal-address` is set; when it is, the challenger logs once at startup and clears invalidated proofs on every L1 head, alongside bond claiming.

**How:** A new `game/withdrawals` scheduler runs beside the bond claimer and gets the same games list. For each game that resolved `CHALLENGER_WINS` it filters `WithdrawalProvenExtension1` logs from the game's `l1Head` block, batch-reads `provenWithdrawals` for the pairs it finds, and sends a delete for each one still recorded against that game. Deleted rows read back with a zero timestamp, which makes this idempotent; an in-memory per-game cursor keeps later heads to the new blocks only.

**For reviewers:** anyone can prove many cheap withdrawals against a game the challenger will win, making the challenger pay unrewarded gas to delete them all — hence off unless the portal address is set, and capped at 100 deletes per game per head. Unit tests only, no e2e or action-test coverage.
